` should trigger this. Let me think about why the PoC didn't crash. Maybe the issue is that the buffer isn't being filled to exactly `q` before the `&` is encountered. Let me reconsider. Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the `fxUTF8Buffer` check more carefully. The check is: ```c if (string + mxStringByteLength(character) > limit) { ``` For a single-byte character, `mxStringByteLength(character)` returns 1. So the check is `string + 1 > limit`, i.e., `string >= limit`. But `limit = q = buffer + bufferSize - 1`. So when `string == q`, the check is `q + 1 > q` → true → memory error. So after writing `bufferSize - 1 = 65535` characters, `p = q`. The next `fxUTF8Buffer` call would trigger the memory error. But in my PoC, the 65536th character is `&`, which is handled by the `case '&':` branch, not the `default` branch. So `fxGetNextEntity` is called with `p = q`. In `fxGetNextEntity`: - `*p++ = '&'` writes at `q` (valid), `p = q+1` - `fxGetNextCharacter` reads `#` - `*p++ = '#'` writes at `q+1` (OOB) This should trigger ASAN. But it didn't crash. Let me think about why. Hmm, maybe the issue is that the buffer isn't actually being filled to `q`. Let me reconsider. Maybe the `fxUTF8Buffer` for the 65535th character doesn't advance `p` to `q` as I expect. Actually, wait. Let me reconsider. The buffer starts at `p = parser->buffer`. Each `fxUTF8Buffer` call writes one character and returns `p + 1`. After N characters, `p = buffer + N`. After 65535 characters, `p = buffer + 65535 = q`. The check for the 65535th character: `string = buffer + 65534`, `string + 1 = buffer + 65535 = q`, `q > q` → false. So no error, write happens at `buffer + 65534`, `p = buffer + 65535 = q`. Then the 65536th character is `&`. It's handled by `case '&':` which calls `fxGetNextEntity(parser, p, q)` with `p = q`. In `fxGetNextEntity`: - `*p++ = '&'` writes at `q` (valid), `p = q+1` - `fxGetNextCharacter` reads `#` - `*p++ = '#'` writes at `q+1` (OOB) This should be a heap-buffer-overflow. But it didn't crash. ` isn't valid JSX syntax in this parser, or the parser handles it differently. Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the issue is that the parser doesn't reach the JSX child parsing because of some other error first. Let me check if there's a simpler way to test. Actually, let me reconsider the whole approach. Maybe the buffer isn't 64KB in the actual fuzz target. Let me check if there's a different buffer size being used. Wait, looking at `fuzz_oss`: ```c xsCreation _creation = { ... 64 * 1024, /* parserBufferSize */ ... }; ``` So the parser buffer is 64KB = 65536 bytes. That's what I assumed. Let me think about another possibility. Maybe the issue is that the `&` character in the JSX child text isn't being processed by `fxGetNextEntity` because the buffer is already full and `fxUTF8Buffer` for the last 'a' character triggered a memory error that longjmps out. Wait, let me re-examine. After writing 65535 'a' characters, `p = q`. The next character is `&`. In `fxGetNextTokenJSXChild`, the switch statement: ```c case '&': p = fxGetNextEntity(parser, p, q); break; ``` So `fxGetNextEntity` is called with `p = q`. This should work as I described. Hmm, but maybe the issue is that the parser doesn't even reach the JSX child parsing. Let me check if maybe the `const x =
` syntax causes a parse error before reaching the child text. Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the issue is that the JSX element name parsing or attribute parsing fails. Let me check `fxJSXElementName`: ```c void fxJSXElementName(txParser* parser) { txInteger line = parser->line; txSymbol* symbol = parser->symbol; fxGetNextToken(parser); if (parser->token == XS_TOKEN_COLON) { ... } ... } ``` After `fxGetNextToken(parser)` in `fxJSXElement`, the token should be `XS_TOKEN_IDENTIFIER` for `div`. Then `fxJSXElementName` is called. This should work. Then the loop checks for attributes. The next token after `div` would be `>` (XS_TOKEN_MORE), which breaks the loop. Then since `!closed`, it enters the child parsing loop. Let me try a different approach. Maybe I should test with a smaller input first to verify the JSX parsing works. Maybe the issue is that the buffer size in the actual compiled binary is different, or maybe the `fxUTF8Buffer` behavior is different than I think.
